summary:
Reality tier: a cloud container, test keys, no founder device, VEPMC 0. No bubblewrap, no Playwright for Python, no macOS.

The core claim holds here, on the production path. On pr196 a founder-signed mission whose check is browser.render spends 45.4 s in its first tick, is refused and never closes. On the branch (46ab6f89) the same mission is ACHIEVED and appraised VERIFIED in two ticks (3.1 s), also on the merge with compose-20261111b. The check contacts no host: zero AF_INET syscalls for the real headless shell and for the real full Chrome, zero connections on 127.0.0.1:9, and the browser gets only HOME, LANG and PATH. Nothing in the change grants, attaches, restores or dispatches: after a founder detach, a passing check changes nothing across ticks and a restart.

What needs fixing before this is called done:
1. On a confined-egress body the check runs a browser outside GREG's namespace, even where the confined route then refuses for lack of bubblewrap. pr196 started no browser there.
2. The check uses the unconfined sandbox rule for a render that will run confined, so a browser that works only with --no-sandbox is refused before the confined route is reached (stand-in; real host not reproduced).
3. The manifest names the first installed candidate at import and the office's precheck reads it. When that build is replaced while the body runs, browser.render is UNAVAILABLE and the founder gets a SENSOR_FAILURE ask, although chrome_binary() returns a working browser. The branch makes that name a versioned Playwright directory.
4. Pre-existing on pr196, not introduced: with GREG_CHROMIUM naming a working browser other than the default, the mission is ACHIEVED but appraised REFUTED, because the appraiser's environment is stripped and it derives another manifest digest.
5. 12 of 13 reviewer mutants survive the builder's test file; 10 survive both browser test files.
6. A 4-line baseline (candidate order only) passes the same real-browser tests and closes the same mission here. The check and memory are shown to matter only with stand-ins.

Probes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/ . Outputs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-out/ . My worktrees (all detached, the builder's untouched): adv-br (46ab6f89), adv-br-196 (pr196), adv-br-compose (compose-20261111b), adv-br-merge (scratch merge commit 9c76468e, local only) under the same scratchpad.

findings.title: On a confined-egress body the check starts a browser outside the namespace, even when the confined route then refuses
findings.claim: The builder says "No change to the signed target, the egress rules, the relay path or any authority file". _render_behind_relay's own rule is "without namespaces nothing runs". On the branch browser_render calls chrome_binary() before it looks at ctx.egress, so every candidate's check runs unconfined (and with --no-sandbox as root) on a body configured for confined egress. The allowlist justification for cannot_render does not say so.
findings.reproduction: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-196 (then .../adv-br) && GREG_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1243/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/confined_probe.py . It calls the real browser_render with ctx.egress set to a relay object and logs every subprocess.run. This container has no bubblewrap.
findings.observed_output: pr196 8d205324: CapabilityError "confined egress needs bubblewrap network namespaces here", browser processes started: none. Branch 46ab6f89: the same CapabilityError, but first one process started: argv0 chrome-headless-shell, --no-sandbox true, bwrap false, page data:text/html. The process renders a constant page and made no AF_INET syscall, so the exposure is the browser binary running outside the namespace that hides the founder's home and the body's keys and ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: When ctx.egress is set, check that namespaces work before choosing a binary, and either run the check inside the same no-network namespace or do not judge at all on that route. Say in the allowlist justification where the check runs.

findings.title: The check applies the unconfined sandbox rule to a render that will run confined
findings.claim: The commit says the check uses "the render's own command line, environment and sandbox rule". The confined render always adds --no-sandbox (sandboxed = _sandboxes_itself() and ctx.egress is None). The check adds it only as root. A browser that cannot create its own sandbox as an ordinary user is refused before the confined route is tried. pr196 reached the confined route with it.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br-196 (then .../adv-br) && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/confined_rule.py . Stand-in browser that renders only with --no-sandbox, ordinary-user rule forced, ctx.egress set, _render_behind_relay replaced by a recorder that runs the argv directly (no bubblewrap here).
findings.observed_output: pr196: confined_render_reached_with_no_sandbox [true], "rendered inside the namespace route (os_sandboxed=False)". Branch: confined_render_reached_with_no_sandbox [], "REFUSED: no installed browser renders a page here: chrome-needs-no-sandbox did not render a local page: No usable sandbox!". The logic is shown with a stand-in. A real host where Chrome refuses its own sandbox for an ordinary user was not reproduced (this container runs as root).
findings.suggested_fix: Give the check the rule of the route it serves (pass whether the render will be confined), or judge inside the namespace.

findings.title: The manifest names an import-time path that the office's precheck gates on; a replaced build strands browser.render on a running body
findings.claim: The builder lists "manifest binaries entry changes where a Playwright headless shell is installed" as a limitation without its consequence. binaries=(installed_chrome(),) is fixed at import. AuthorityOffice.precheck calls manifest.available() on it. The branch selects the real binary at call time, so the two can disagree. On pr196 in this container the manifest named /usr/bin/google-chrome, which survives Playwright upgrades; on the branch it names chromium_headless_shell-1243/..., a directory whose name changes with every build.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/upgrade_probe.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-out/upgrade (same on .../adv-br-merge). Simulation, stated: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS is pointed at a temp root holding a copy of the real headless-shell wrapper as build 1300, and the manifest's binaries are set to installed_chrome(), which is what import computes on such a machine. Then build 1300 is replaced by 1301 while the Body runs, and a signed mission with a browser.render check is ticked four times. Digests: mission_probe.py prints them on each tree.
findings.observed_output: manifest_names <root>/pw/chromium_headless_shell-1300/...; chrome_binary_now <root>/pw/chromium_headless_shell-1301/... (a working browser); registry_usable false "binary ... not installed or not executable"; four observations "sensor UNAVAILABLE: binary ..."; achieved false; open request SENSOR_FAILURE "the mission cannot measure its success checks". Same on the merged tree. Manifest digest on this container: pr196 sha256:c528d73fac882532 (/usr/bin/google-chrome), branch sha256:2e73a0cbbcf4029d (headless shell), so the upgrade itself changes it. Mission Control's health for browser.render is the same manifest.available(), so it also does not show what the check learned.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the declared and the run binary one thing: either keep a stable declaration in the manifest and let precheck for browser.render ask the call-time candidates, or drop the versioned path from the manifest. Add a Body test where the first candidate changes while the body runs.

findings.title: Founder's choice on the production path: the mission is ACHIEVED but appraised REFUTED (pre-existing on pr196, not introduced)
findings.claim: The claim is that the founder's GREG_CHROMIUM choice is honoured. It is, for the render. But the body process builds the browser.render manifest with GREG_CHROMIUM in its environment, and Body.appraise starts the appraiser with a stripped environment (PATH, LANG, PYTHONPATH). The appraiser re-derives payload_hash from its own BUILTINS manifest digest (greg/appraisal.py _invocation_receipt_bound), which names another binary. The builder's tests exercise the founder's choice only at function level.
findings.reproduction: cp the headless-shell wrapper to .../scratchpad/adv-br-out/founder-bin/founders-chrome ; cd .../scratchpad/adv-br && GREG_CHROMIUM=.../adv-br-out/founder-bin/founders-chrome python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/mission_probe.py .../adv-br-out/m_branch_choice 6 . Same command in .../adv-br-196. Control: GREG_CHROMIUM set to the default first candidate.
findings.observed_output: Branch: tick 1 achieved true, appraised ["REFUTED"], finding "c: receipt not bound to this closure and signed sensor". pr196 with the same variable: achieved true, appraised REFUTED, same finding. Control (choice equals the default candidate): VERIFIED. Without the variable on the branch: VERIFIED. So any difference between the first candidate the body saw at import and the one a later appraiser process sees turns a closure REFUTED; the branch makes that first candidate a versioned Playwright path.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the appraisal to the manifest digest the dispatch recorded, or hand the appraiser the same binary choice. Add a Body-level test of a founder-chosen browser through appraisal.

findings.title: 12 of 13 reviewer mutants survive the builder's test file; 10 survive both browser test files
findings.claim: The builder reports the mutation gate 25/25 caught (true, re-run here, 1 m 42 s, and 25/25 on the merged tree). The project standard is that every safeguard has a test that fails without it. These unlisted mutants of the new code leave tests/unit/test_greg_browser_binary.py at 14 passed.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/extra_mutants.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br (uses scripts/ci/mutation_harness.py on a scratch copy; every old string occurs once). Each survivor was then re-run to confirm "14 passed", and run against tests/unit/test_greg_browser.py with and without GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1.
findings.observed_output: 1/13 caught. Survivors: R1 _executable without is_file (a directory counts as a browser); R2 _executable without X_OK; R3 key without mtime; R4 key without size; R5 "cannot be read" turned into a raise; R6 check without cwd=profile; R7 _sandboxes_itself returns True always; R8 render timeout x10000; R9 render timeout no longer a CapabilityError; R10 manifest binaries not from installed_chrome(); R11 non-numeric build sorted first; R12 --disable-background-networking replaced. Caught: R13 retry clock. Against the real-browser file: R1-R6, R8, R9, R11, R12 give 3 passed; R7 and R10 give "1 passed, 2 skipped" as CI runs it and "2 errors" only with GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1, which no workflow sets (grep finds it only in the test file). Vacuity: with greg/capabilities.py and greg/computer.py reverted to pr196, the 14 stand-in tests give 14 errors at fixture setup (AttributeError PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS): none passes vacuously, none is a behavioural failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add stand-in tests for a directory and a non-executable file as candidates, same-size and same-mtime replacement, a vanished candidate, the check's cwd, the real _sandboxes_itself body, a render (not check) that never returns, and the manifest's binaries. Set GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 in a CI job that has a browser, or remove the knob.

findings.title: "The founder's choice is never replaced" is false for five of ten ways the variable can be set
findings.claim: The CI step name says "the founder's choice is never replaced" and the test is named test_the_founders_choice_is_never_replaced_by_another_browser. The commit message is more careful ("when it names an executable"). When GREG_CHROMIUM is set but does not name an executable file, GREG silently runs another browser. pr196 behaved the same.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/founder_choice.py (real browser_render on a loopback page; logs every binary run).
findings.observed_output: Only the chosen binary ran for: a working absolute path (rendered), a broken executable (REFUSED "broken-chrome did not render a local page: broken"), a relative path that exists from the cwd (REFUSED "my-chrome could not be started (No such file or directory)"). Another browser (chrome-headless-shell) was run and RENDERED for: a directory, a non-executable file, a missing path, an unexpanded ~/chrome, a relative path that does not resolve from the cwd, a working path with a trailing newline. The empty string also falls back, which reads as unset.
findings.suggested_fix: When GREG_CHROMIUM is non-empty and does not name an absolute executable file, refuse and name it. Or change the wording of the step, the test and the docstring.

findings.title: The real-browser evidence does not separate the mechanism from a 4-line baseline
findings.claim: The fail-before/pass-after evidence (both real-browser tests skip on pr196, pass on the branch) is offered for a 142-line change with a check and a memory. A baseline that only puts the Playwright headless shell first and matches chrome-linux* does as well in this container.
findings.reproduction: Baseline diff: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-out/baseline.diff (4 changed lines in chrome_binary on pr196). On a copy of pr196 with it and the branch's test file: GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_greg_browser.py ; then mission_probe.py. Ablation of the headless shell on the branch: python .../adv-br-probes/no_shell_time.py from .../adv-br.
findings.observed_output: Baseline: 3 passed in 4.08 s; mission ACHIEVED and VERIFIED at tick 1, same manifest digest as the branch. What the check and memory add, measured with this container's real browsers and the headless shell hidden: candidates google-chrome and chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome both hang; branch call 1 takes 91.6 s and refuses naming both, call 2 takes 0.0 s; pr196 and the baseline take 45 s on every call. The case "first installed browser cannot render, a later one can" exists only in the stand-in tests.
findings.suggested_fix: State the comparison in the PR. Keep the check if the fast refusal and the fall-through are wanted, but name the stand-in tests as its only evidence.

findings.title: A build directory name with a non-decimal digit makes greg.capabilities unimportable
findings.claim: The commit says the manifest names the first installed candidate "without running anything at import". Import now also parses build directory names: playwright_builds uses str.isdigit() then int(), and isdigit() is true for characters int() refuses.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br-196 (then .../adv-br) && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/import_crash.py . glob.glob is replaced before the import so the listing holds /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1243²/...; nothing on disk is touched. Running-body variant: odd_dir_running.py.
findings.observed_output: pr196: the import succeeds. Branch: "ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '1243²'" raised by import greg.capabilities, so no GREG process (body, appraiser, CLI) would start. When the name appears after a body has started: ticks do not raise; each scheduled observation is "sensor UNCERTAIN: executor raised ValueError", 6 dispatches without receipts, mission blocked, one SENSOR_FAILURE ask. Writing under /opt/pw-browsers needs root in this image.
findings.suggested_fix: Use isdecimal() or catch ValueError and sort such a directory last.

findings.title: The memory keys on the path the candidate names, which here is a wrapper script; a success is kept when the real binary changes
findings.claim: The claim is that a success is remembered "until the binary changes". The key is (path, size, mtime) of the candidate path. In this container both first candidates are shell wrappers: the Playwright headless shell is a 198-byte script that execs chrome-headless-shell.real, and /usr/bin/google-chrome is a 95-byte script that execs /opt/pw-browsers/chromium.
findings.observed_output: wrapper_real_binary_replaced: first null (renders); after the real binary is replaced by one that hangs, cannot_render returns null in 0.0 s without running it. same_size_same_mtime: not judged again. symlink_retargeted: judged again (clean). two_renders_at_once: check_runs 2 (no lock; cost only, and inside one body renders are serialized by the turn). growth: 20 entries after 20 reinstalls of one path; nothing is removed. A stale success degrades to pr196 behaviour (a 45 s timeout per render, no fall-through) until restart. A render that times out never updates the memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Forget a remembered success when a render with that binary times out or fails to start.

findings.title: The first render blocks the body's turn 45 s per non-rendering candidate, again every ten minutes
findings.claim: browser.render runs inline in Body.tick (on compose only worker.commission is a background capability). The check adds up to 45 s per candidate before the render's own 45 s. pr196 spent at most 45 s per call.
findings.reproduction: cd .../scratchpad/adv-br && python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f78643ba-8a14-5107-b25c-e0462dfdc774/scratchpad/adv-br-probes/no_shell_time.py (real browsers, headless shell hidden). Deadlines read in greg/acceptance.py (STALE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 180), greg/service.py (TimeoutStopSec=30), policy/consequence_gate.py (grant expiry checked at commit), greg/authority.py (passport ttl 900 s).
findings.observed_output: Two hanging candidates: call 1 = 91.6 s. No caller deadline breaks at 90 s: the grant is checked before the adapter runs, the passport lives 900 s, the appraiser does not re-run browser.render (not in REOBSERVABLE). Four non-rendering candidates would reach the 180 s rule under which the console, Mission Control and acceptance call the body not running; not reproduced. One transient failure of a working browser also removes it for ten minutes (the builder's own test asserts the single run). _render_behind_relay keeps a literal timeout=45 while the error text reads RENDER_SECONDS.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the total time one call may spend judging, and report the remaining candidates as not yet judged.

findings.title: browser.session's chromium() now drives another path, and newest-by-number is not shown to be the right build
findings.claim: The builder says the session route "finds the full browser under either directory spelling, newest build first, and never the headless shell". Not exercised: Playwright for Python is not installed.
findings.reproduction: In .../scratchpad/adv-br-196 and .../adv-br: python -c "from greg import computer; print(computer.chromium())"; then a temp root with builds 1187, 1243, 1250 and a directory named chromium-1255/chrome-linux64/chrome.
findings.observed_output: pr196: /usr/bin/google-chrome. Branch: /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome (the same real binary here, without the wrapper; computer.py adds --no-sandbox itself). With several builds the branch returns the highest number, and returns the directory chromium-1255/.../chrome because chromium() tests os.access(X_OK) only. A Playwright driver expects the one build its own version pins; whether it can drive a newer one was not tested. chromium() does not read GREG_CHROMIUM on either tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Use _executable in chromium(). Decide the build from the installed Playwright version, or record this as unverified.

findings.title: Scope of two statements: where Playwright installs, and the no-browser refusal
findings.claim: (a) The comment says PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS = "/opt/pw-browsers" is "where Playwright installs its browser builds". (b) The commit says no browser installed is now a CapabilityError where before it was a FileNotFoundError the Gate records as unknown.
findings.reproduction: echo $PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH in this container; read greg/authority.py line 119 (precheck before the cone) and the upgrade probe's observations.
findings.observed_output: (a) /opt/pw-browsers is this image's PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH. The code does not read that variable or Playwright's default cache directory, so the headless-shell preference has no effect on a body that installed Playwright the default way. Same root as pr196. (b) Through the office, a manifest whose binary is missing is answered UNAVAILABLE by precheck before the adapter runs (measured in the upgrade probe), on both trees. The new CapabilityError is reached by a direct adapter call or a binary removed between precheck and the call. Skip count: I reproduce 181 passed, 1 failed with 18 skipped; 19 with tests/unit/test_greg_computer.py added.
findings.suggested_fix: Word both statements to their scope.

checked_and_clean: Fail-before on pr196 8d205324, re-run: tests/unit/test_greg_browser.py gives 1 passed, 2 skipped in 92.78 s (both skips: "browser did not finish rendering within 45 seconds"). Branch 46ab6f89 with GREG_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1: test_greg_browser.py and test_greg_browser_binary.py give 17 passed in 12.13 s. The three real tests include the isolation checks (only the signed host reachable), so those hold with the headless shell.

Production path through Body.tick (mission_probe.py): pr196 tick 0 takes 45.4 s, observation "sensor REFUSED: capability refused: browser did not finish rendering within 45 seconds", not achieved in 4 ticks. Branch: ACHIEVED and appraised VERIFIED at tick 1, 3.1 s wall, receipts name chrome-headless-shell. Merged tree (through #290/#291): the same.

The check contacts no host. Real headless shell under strace -f: no AF_INET connect, sendto or sendmsg; only AF_UNIX to /run/dbus/system_bus_socket and AF_NETLINK. Real full Chrome for its whole 45.26 s: the same. A listener bound on 127.0.0.1:9 (the check's proxy address) accepted 0 connections in both runs.

The check does not see the caller's environment. strace -v of execve: the browser receives HOME, LANG, PATH (and PWD from sh); the caller had 176 variables including a planted GREG_SECRET_FOR_PROBE and HTTPS_PROXY.

Authority (authority_probe.py, branch and merged tree): after a founder CAPABILITY_DETACH of browser.render, a check that passes in the same process changes nothing. State stays DETACHED over 3 ticks and a restart; the only capability.state record is the founder's; grants 0, dispatches 0, receipts 0; the mission starts 0 browser processes. cannot_render writes nothing to the ledger.
python -m governance.integrity --check on the branch: 13 protected artifacts, all as authorized. The diff touches no protected artifact.

A changed binaries tuple cannot detach, quarantine or refuse browser.render by itself: attach state is keyed by capability id; genesis.is_capability_fault returns False for a capability Genesis did not form; Genesis.restore handles formed capabilities only; AuthorityOffice._same_manifest compares objects from one process's BUILTINS.
No leftover processes or check profiles after four real 45 s timeouts of the full Chrome; TemporaryDirectory cleanup raised nothing.

No ledger flood: a refused or unavailable browser.render observation is recorded once per scheduled wake (1 in 4 ticks at 1 s steps on pr196; 4 in 4 ticks at 4000 s steps), the same engine path as before.

A symlinked candidate whose target changes is judged again. Paths with spaces work: a stand-in at .../Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome is chosen and rendered (argv is a list), and the builder's 14 tests pass under a --basetemp containing a space.

The allowlist sentence is true in the product: cannot_render is called only by chrome_binary, chrome_binary only by browser_render; installed_chrome() at import runs nothing. tests/unit/test_effect_call_allowlist.py passes.
Builder's mutation gate: 25/25 caught on the branch and 25/25 on the merged tree; no stale anchor.

Composition: git merge of 46ab6f89 onto compose-20261111b has one conflict, .github/workflows/canonical-ci.yml (both sides append job-10 steps); resolved by keeping all four steps; YAML parses. Merged tree: test_greg_browser, test_greg_browser_binary, test_effect_call_allowlist, test_greg_authority_attach_state, test_greg_authority_registered_identity, test_greg_capabilities, test_greg_egress, test_resource_bounds, test_greg_retained_receipt, test_greg_retained_receipt_history, test_greg_faithful_text: 208 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 skipped. Unmerged compose: 192 passed, 2 skipped (the two real-browser tests), the same xfail. test_greg_background_dispatch, test_greg_handoff_evidence, test_greg_retained_receipt_process, test_greg_body_supervised and the route's neighbours on the merged tree: 57 passed, 19 skipped, 46 failed; all 46 are tests/unit/test_genomes_formal_b.py for a missing numpy and fail identically on unmerged compose.

Neighbours on the branch (capabilities, egress, faithful_text, computer, relay_door, mcp_remote_words, mcp_token, confined_egress, ebfc5f7_review, acceptance, both browser files): 152 passed, 19 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is the known container failure in tests/integration/test_greg_acceptance.py.

Claims that match: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 for both binaries; the Playwright directory is chrome-linux64; 14 stand-in tests; the check takes 0.43 s for the headless shell; refusal text names each candidate and why.

Closing list on the branch: test_repo_health_gates, test_effect_call_allowlist, test_governance_integrity, test_greg_packaging, test_sources_parse, test_import_layering: 115 passed. python -m acceptance check: sound. python -m acceptance directive --against 8d20532464b1533b28d71d8331ca3412a90dbb11: exit 0, "the pinned asks hold".
not_checked: The confined (relay) render with real bubblewrap: whether the headless shell renders inside the namespace with only its parent directory re-shown, and what a check run outside says about inside. No bubblewrap here. Skipped tests that matter to this: tests/unit/test_foundry_relay_door.py (7), tests/integration/test_greg_mcp_token.py (2), tests/integration/test_greg_confined_egress.py (bubblewrap skips at lines 371, 571, 696, 724, 761, 887, 930).

browser.session and Playwright for Python: chromium() was only evaluated, never used to drive a browser. Skipped: tests/unit/test_greg_computer.py (1), tests/integration/test_greg_confined_egress.py:444 (2).
A real host where Chrome cannot create its sandbox as an ordinary user (the trigger of the second finding). Shown with a stand-in only.

A real replacement of a build under /opt/pw-browsers. The directory is shared with other workers, so the upgrade was simulated with a temp install root and the manifest set to what import computes there.

A pr196-to-branch upgrade with a browser.render receipt retained before it and appraised after. The digest change is measured; the REFUTED consequence is inferred from the founder's-choice measurement of the same comparison.
macOS, the founder's Chromebook, a GitHub runner. Whether the full Chrome binary hangs anywhere else is not known.
time.monotonic across suspend: not run. By reading, CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux and mach_absolute_time on macOS do not advance while suspended, so the ten-minute window counts awake time only.
A candidate that writes unbounded output for 45 s (capture_output holds it in memory), and Chrome managed policies that override the proxy flags.
The full suite. Tests that need networkx, scipy, z3, ortools, sympy or numpy skip or fail in this container.
